correctness.rationale: Each pair of independent eccentric-anomaly differences is uniform on a circle before a positive-definite diagonal affine map. Conditional on a given first vertex, the two chord directions are independent uniform directions over the same semicircle. Their difference has an exactly triangular density; averaging the semicircle rotation makes their angular midpoint uniform independently of the difference. The mapped dot-product sign is cos(delta)+tau*cos(2m), and its negative probability integrates to an arccos-square moment. The arcsin-square generating series is proved from the arcsine-square differential equation and the central binomial trigonometric moment, giving 1/2 Li_2(tau^2). A Euclidean triangle has at most one obtuse angle and right angles have probability zero. The asserted asymptotic constants follow from the convergent dilogarithm expansion and its reflection identity. The included standalone standard-library checker independently corroborated six quadrature identities and 5x85000 direct geometric simulations; finite tests are not used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp comparator is the publicly solved 2018 off-center circle triangle-containment probability. It shares exactly the same dilogarithm *function* after mapping its radial parameter to ellipse anisotropy, and this known result is expressly credited. However the random event there is containment of a displaced fixed point by three points of a circle; here it is acute Euclidean angles after affinely transforming the random vertices. These events are not pointwise equal under the shared uniform-circle parameterization. The present theorem proves their probability equality by a distinct random-chord-direction computation; it is not merely a claim that the dilogarithm itself is novel. Modern primary papers on random spherical polytopes, ellipse triangle center loci, and area-uniform disc triangles do not state this affine-uniform ellipse law. Historical uniqueness is not certified.
residual_risks: The 2018 circle-containment problem has exactly the same dilogarithm profile, so a broader yet unlocated probabilistic equivalence or affine transfer theorem may imply the ellipse statement.

value.rationale: Euclidean acuteness is a fundamental shape statistic, and the affine pushforward of uniform circle data is a canonical sampling law for anisotropic ellipse boundaries. The result completely classifies this statistic for all semiaxes (not just a pointwise example), proves strict circular optimality, obtains a nonanalytic logarithmic degeneracy rate, and identifies an unexpected equality with a previously studied geometric probability under a precise parameter correspondence. The exact function was known in the other model, and the legitimate new object and link are explicitly stated; no broad unfounded applications are claimed.
